newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS SLALOM GOLD FOR ITALY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS SLALOM GOLD FOR ITALY.

text.p: Italy's Deborah Compagnoni, who had not won an Alpine skiing slalom before this season, took world championship gold in the discipline on Wednesday ahead of compatriot Lara Magoni.

Compagnoni, second after the first leg, clocked a total time of one minute 43.88 seconds down the Kandahar piste to become her country's first-ever women's slalom world champion and secure the fourth gold of her 10-year career.

Magoni, who had started the second leg in seventh place, took silver in 1:45.15 after several of the frontrunners crashed out on the icy piste bathed by floodlights. Switzerland's Karin Roten, the first leg leader, was third in 1:45.48.
Double Olympic champion Compagnoni was just 0.05 seconds behind Roten after the first leg and was by far the fastest in the second 62-gate leg, set by a Swede.
Defending champion Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden, ninth after the first leg, attacked a touch too aggressively in the second and went crashing out after missing a gate.
She was the first of a string of favourites to fall.

Sabine Egger of Austria fell almost immediately and Austrian-born Claudia Riegler, who skis for New Zealand and has won three World Cup slaloms this season, followed her after hooking the fourth gate and sliding down the piste.
Marlies Oester, another Swiss medal hope after finishing the first leg fourth, also crashed out.
